title: Start the Physical Section Properly
objective: Choose one physical activity for the award's physical section, set a starting measure you can repeat, and write the first week of the log with the days already booked.

blocks.text: LAUNCH · ASDAN · Week 5. Enrichment Award, physical section. Start the Physical Section Properly.
Objective: choose one physical activity for the award's physical section, set a starting measure you can repeat, and write the first week of the log with the days already booked.
Success evidence: one activity chosen, a repeatable starting measure recorded, and three dated sessions booked in the log.
Activities come from the approved list. Nothing here is about body size, weight or appearance.
40 minutes. Offline.

stages.title: Arrival · retrieve

blocks.text: The physical section is about a record, not a result
The award does not ask you to be good at anything.
It asks you to do a physical activity regularly for a set number of weeks and to record it.
Somebody who starts slow and keeps the log completes the section.
Somebody very fit who records nothing does not.
So the log is the work, and today we set it up so it is easy to keep.
Say plainly that nothing here is about weight or appearance, and keep the conversation on the measure and the log.
You need the approved activity list, a stopwatch or a counter, and the twelve-week log sheet.
Twelve weeks is the length of this section, so the thing you choose has to survive twelve weeks.
That is the only real constraint, and it rules out most of the impressive answers.
The list has fourteen activities on it and none of them need equipment you do not have.

stages.data-ta1: Activity list out first. Measures come after the choice, never before it.
stages.data-ta2: If a pupil raises weight or appearance, name the rule once and turn the conversation to the measure.

blocks.text: Two starting measures
Measure A: I am quite unfit at the moment.
Measure B: walked the school perimeter twice in nine minutes and forty seconds, on the eleventh of October.
Twelve weeks from now, only one of these can be repeated.
A repeatable measure has a thing done, a number, and a date.
Without all three you will have no way to show the section did anything.

items: 1 · pick the activity from the list.
2 · pick something you can count or time.
3 · do it once and write the number.

blocks.text: Read measure A again and try to write down how you would repeat it in December.
You cannot, and that is the whole reason the measure needs a number and a date.
The date matters as much as the number. A number with no date cannot be compared to anything.

stages.title: I Do · model

blocks.text: Choosing, measuring, booking
I take walking from the list, because I can do it without booking a space.
Now the measure. It has to be the same every time, so I choose the perimeter, twice, timed.
Same route, same number of laps, same stopwatch. Only the time changes.
I do it once today and write nine minutes forty, with the date.
Then the three sessions. Tuesday lunch, Thursday lunch, Sunday morning.

blocks.caption: Booking the sessions is what makes the log get filled in
blocks.title: Starting the physical section
blocks.alt: Four boxes joined by arrows: choose the activity, set the measure, record it, book three sessions

blocks.text: Booked days, not intentions. Twice a week is a plan; regularly is not.
If a booked day is missed, that goes in the log too, with the reason.
Insist on real days and times. A log with no booked days is filled in for the first fortnight and then abandoned.
Notice I chose the activity for its convenience, not for how it sounds.
Convenience is what gets a log filled in, and a filled log is what completes the section.
I write the route down as well as the time, because in twelve weeks I will not remember which way I went.

stages.data-ta1: Model with a genuinely undemanding activity. Pupils copy the level they see modelled.

stages.title: We Do · everyone commits

blocks.text: Sort the measures
Six measure cards are on your table. Sort them into repeatable and not repeatable.
Two laps of the field, timed. Feeling fitter. Twenty step-ups in one minute.
Doing more than last week. Ten lengths of the hall. Getting less out of breath.
Then match each repeatable one to what you would need to measure it.
When your table is done, hold up the one you argued about most.
One card has a number in it and is still not repeatable. Say which, and what is missing.

stages.data-ta1: Cards sorted first. Nobody holds anything up until every table has finished.

stages.title: I Do 2 · connect

blocks.text: Why the first number should be easy
People set a hard first measure to look serious, and then dread repeating it.
A first measure you can do on a bad week is the one that gets repeated.
And repeating it is the only thing the section actually requires.
Choose something you could do today if you had slept badly, and start there.

blocks.caption: The section is completed by the log, not by the first number
blocks.title: Setting the first measure
blocks.alt: Two boxes compared: an easy first measure produces a full log, a hard one produces gaps

blocks.text: You can always add a second, harder measure later, and many people do.
You cannot go back and fill in the weeks you skipped.
Write the missed sessions in the log as well as the completed ones. A gap with a reason is still a record.
A second measure added in week six is a good sign. A first measure abandoned in week three is not.

stages.data-ta1: Steer anyone setting an ambitious first measure towards something they could do tired.

stages.title: We Do 2 · lab

blocks.text: Could I repeat yours?
Work in twos. Read your partner your measure.
They say whether they could repeat it exactly from what you said.
If they could not, they name the missing piece: the route, the count, or the timing.
Add the missing piece and read it again.
Then swap over and do the same for theirs.
Read only the measure, not the reason. If the measure needs the reason to make sense, it is not finished.
If they could repeat it, say so and stop. There is no mark for making the measure more complicated.

stages.data-ta1: Pair by table. Two and a half minutes each way, timed aloud.

stages.title: Independent · evidence

blocks.text: Activity, measure, and three booked days
Work on your own. Write your activity and why you chose it.
Write your measure so that somebody else could repeat it exactly.
Do it once if the space allows, and write the number and today's date.
Then book three sessions with real days and times in the log.
If you finish early, write what you will do if you miss one.

items: Supported · choose an activity and record a measure with support.
Standard · choose an activity, record a repeatable measure with the date, and book three sessions.
Stretch · as Standard, and write what you will do if you miss a booked session.

blocks.text: Write your three days as dates, not as weekdays. Tuesday recurs; the fourteenth does not.
Book the first session for this week if you can. A section that starts next week usually starts the week after.
Say your measure out loud before you write it. Anything you cannot say in one breath is too complicated.
Put the log somewhere you will see it on a booked day, not somewhere safe.

stages.data-ta1: Scribe exactly. Do not upgrade a pupil's measure into a more impressive one.
stages.data-ta2: A pupil who cannot do the measure today records the plan and the date they will do it.

stages.title: Exit · Audience and Influence

blocks.text: Read the measure to an adult
Read your measure to the adult at your table.
They read it back and say whether they could repeat it from your words alone.
If they could not, add the missing detail now.
Then choose what happens next: start this week, start next week, or change the activity.
Write that choice in the log with today's date before you leave.
The log goes in the award folder and comes out at the start of every session from now on.
If you change the activity, keep the old page in the log rather than tearing it out.

stages.data-ta1: The named adult reads the measure back word for word and says whether it is repeatable.

sections: The measure, and three booked days
